en.title: Iran refuses enriched uranium export threatens US bases in Europe
en.dek: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei stated enriched nuclear material will not leave the country citing a US reward offer.
facts: Mohsen Rezaei stated enriched nuclear material will not leave the country on 11 November 2026
Iran's government condemned a US $20 million reward for information on its nuclear program on 11 November 2026
Iran's top clerical governing body called for a review of nuclear doctrine on 12 November 2026
US envoys met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on 12 November 2026
body: Iran's top clerical governing body called for a review of the nation's nuclear doctrine on 12 November 2026, according to Iran International and Africanews.
Iran's nuclear envoy stated the country will not export enriched uranium, citing the US reward offer as the reason on 12 November 2026, according to FAZ.
Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei stated on 11 November 2026 that enriched nuclear material will not leave the country, according to Reuters and The Straits Times.
Rezaei also stated on 11 November 2026 that no negotiations are taking place between Tehran and Washington, according to Reuters and The Straits Times.
Iran's military reported four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz on 12 November 2026, according to The Straits Times and DW.com.
France 24 reported that Iran's security chief stated Tehran will strike US bases in Europe if those bases are used to attack Iran on 11 November 2026.
US envoys met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on 12 November 2026, following peace talks in Abu Dhabi, according to Anadolu Ajansı and Al Jazeera.
President Donald Trump said on 12 November 2026 that he does not need a deal with Iran, according to the South China Morning Post and Axios.
en.context: Iran's government condemned a US $20 million reward for information on its nuclear program, according to Daily Sabah. US envoys met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after peace talks in Abu Dhabi, according to Anadolu Ajansı and Al Jazeera.

en.dek: Iran refuses to transfer enriched uranium out of the country following a US reward offer and threatens to target US bases in Europe if attacked.
body: Iranian state media reported military strikes hit Sirik County and Hormozgan province on 10 November 2026, according to reports by Anadolu Ajansı and The Jerusalem Post. Iranian military officials stated on 12 November that four oil tankers were struck by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after entering restricted areas, according to reports by The Straits Times and DW.com.

Iran's top clerical governing body called for a review of the country's nuclear doctrine on 12 November 2026, according to Iran International and Africanews. Iranian nuclear envoys stated that the refusal to export enriched uranium is permanent, citing a US $20 million reward offer for information on Iran's nuclear program as the reason for the stance.

US President Donald Trump stated on 12 November 2026 that he does not need a deal with Iran, according to reports by the South China Morning Post and Axios. Trump directed Vice President J.D. Vance to focus on domestic anti-fraud efforts rather than continuing negotiations with Iranian representatives.

Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei stated on 11 November 2026 that enriched nuclear material will not leave the country, according to Reuters and The Straits Times. Rezaei said that no talks were occurring between Tehran and Washington and warned that Iran would strike US military bases in Europe if those bases were used to attack Iranian territory.

Tehran will not move a single atom of enriched uranium from its territory, an Iranian official stated, according to The Washington Times. Daily Sabah and Yahoo Finance UK reported that the Iranian government condemned the US reward offer and rejected all foreign transfers of its nuclear stockpile.

Diplomatic developments also occurred elsewhere as US envoys met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow following peace talks in Abu Dhabi, according to Anadolu Ajansı and Al Jazeera. Concurrently, the European Parliament reported at least 20,651 confirmed cases of deported Ukrainian children, urging Russia to return them.

body: Der iranische Sicherheitschef Mohsen Rezaei sagte laut Reuters und The Straits Times, dass angereichertes nukleares Material das Land nicht verlassen werde. Rezaei sagte zudem, dass derzeit keine Verhandlungen zwischen Teheran und Washington stattfänden.

Die Erklärung wurde am 11. November 2026 gemeldet. Reuters berichtete, dass Rezaeis Äußerungen während eines öffentlichen Auftritts fielen, bei dem er sich zum Status von Exporten nuklearen Materials äußerte.

Die iranische Regierung verurteilte laut offiziellen iranischen Erklärungen, über die Daily Sabah berichtete, eine US-Belohnung von 20 Millionen US-Dollar für Hinweise auf ihr Atomprogramm. Teheran werde kein einziges Atom angereicherten Urans von seinem Territorium wegbeziehen, erklärte ein iranischer Offizieller.

The Washington Times berichtete am 11. November 2026 über die Aussage zum "einzigen Atom". Die Weigerung erstreckt sich auf alle Exporte angereicherten nuklearen Materials aus iranischem Boden, wie mehrere Medien bestätigten.

Yahoo Finance UK berichtete, dass Rezaei den Transfer von nuklearem Material aus dem Land heraus ablehnte. Der Bericht erschien am 11. November 2026 und deckte sich mit früheren Äußerungen iranischer Offizieller.

The Straits Times bestätigte Rezaeis Haltung zum Verbot des Abtransports von angereichertem Uran über iranische Grenzen hinweg. Sowohl Reuters als auch The Straits Times berichteten am 11. November 2026 über diese Äußerungen.
Daily Sabah berichtete, dass Iran den Transfer von Uran ausschloss und die US-Belohnung verurteilte. Der Bericht stammte vom 11. November 2026.
